findings.reason: the section must state the grammar tightening it inherits from the owner, or the retire needs a compatibility note, because it is a behaviour change it currently denies.
findings.text: the plan's interface account calls the swap "no definition added, one private duplicate retired" as if `_declared_stages` and `declared_section_identities` were the same set, but the retired helper adds typed-record ids and declaration keys unvalidated, while the owner admits them only when `_RESOURCE_SEGMENT_RE.fullmatch` passes, so the swap silently narrows the declared set for a malformed identifier and can turn a ref that resolved before into a `missing-dependency-section` finding after

findings.reason: the three roadmap sites must state whether they read the row or the file-backed resolver, and promotion's fallback must move onto the owner or the section should say why a record-only plan may omit them.
findings.text: every site that asks whether a section exists must reach the one owner, and four still do not: the three staged-ref sites are told to call `declared_section_identities(target)` on the inventory row, but the roadmap already owns a file-aware resolver for rows that lack declarations (`_plan_declarations`, roadmap.py:128, reached through `declared_for`, roadmap.py:290), so a declaration or typed record living only in the plan file still reads as naming no section — the same "one ref resolves while another does not" divergence the section exists to remove; and promotion.py:7273 enumerates a plan's implementable sections (an existence question) yet is left on `plan_section_anchors`, firing exactly when `section_declarations is not a Mapping`, so a plan carrying typed records without a declarations map lists no record section

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the change deepens an interface that already hides the union (gate and comment anchors, declaration keys, typed records) behind one function, and adds no module or parallel surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the census of existence-questions is one short of the owner: three roadmap sites route to the bare owner over a possibly-sparse inventory row while the roadmap's own file-aware resolver exists, and one audited caller, promotion.py:7273, is an existence question left on the narrow anchor function.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1523, cli_options 323, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; the section adds no definition to any family and names in its own text the one private duplicate (`_declared_stages`) it retires, so it satisfies the one rule.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan found the right owner, `declared_section_identities` (reckon/_schema.py:678), and cites the four staged-ref call sites, but treats it as set-equivalent to the helper it retires, `_declared_stages` (roadmap.py:181); the two do not return the same set.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no wrapper is proposed; the design routes callers straight onto the owner, which is the honest extension the rubric asks for.
